answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists sybils by making each identity costly to create. An agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers catch it echoing fake reviews or copying another agent's work. Honest history is tracked like a jade ledger, slow to build and hard to fake, while a prism of independent attestations (uptime, completed trades, dispute outcomes) refracts one identity into many verifiable signals. A sybil farm would need a fresh bond for every puppet, so flooding the market costs more than it earns.
